title: MEASURED BY DELIBERATE INTERVENTION, NOT BY CORRELATION. The lexical-rebind scaffold pre-filter in goal-host-vessel tryL
description: MEASURED BY DELIBERATE INTERVENTION, NOT BY CORRELATION. The lexical-rebind scaffold pre-filter in goal-host-vessel tryLexicalRebind refuses below a ratio of 0.15, and a naturally rephrased goal scores 0.13-0.14 -- it misses by 0.01. Three goals were dispatched with predictions recorded first (validation/reports/PREREG_adaptation_intervention_2026-09-06.md). A: 'Count the number of lines in the file /vessels/activity-api/src/routes/db-admin-repair.ts and report the count' -- reached 381, banked two shellResult donors whose commands contain the path exactly once. B, identical wording with one slot changed to goal-paths.ts: ADAPTATION FIRED -- '[rebind] result for shellResult: selected=true candidates=80' at 04:58:48, the first observed selected=true in this system; it swapped the slot (wc -l <pathA> becomes wc -l <pathB>), returned 1346, matching ground truth, and the value was independently recomputed by a second derivation before acceptance. C, same task and shape but rephrased as 'How many lines does /vessels/activity-api/src/routes/impulses.ts contain?': REFUSED with scaffold-too-weak(0.13)x66 and (0.14)x1. So the mechanism is correct when it fires and is gated out by wording alone. CONTEXT THAT MAKES THIS DECIDABLE: over 24h and 462 rebind calls there were 0 selections; refusals were shape-mismatch 54906, scaffold-too-weak 1762 (median ratio 0.060, max 0.15), slot-gate-rejected 699. Before this intervention the slot gate had rejected 100% of everything reaching it, which argued AGAINST lowering the threshold -- lowering it would only feed a gate that accepts nothing. B falsified that: the slot gate DOES accept a structurally compatible donor. The open question is therefore narrow and empirical: of the candidates scoring 0.10-0.15, how many pass the per-slot literal gate? That is answerable by admitting them and reading the tally, because the literal gate -- not the ratio -- is the correctness guard, as the code's own comment states. THIS IS A POLICY PARAMETER AND THE OPERATOR DELIBERATELY DID NOT CHANGE IT. It was already lowered 0.5 to 0.25 to 0.15, each time from measurement, and 0.15 was chosen as 'the first value below the 0.18 these goals actually score'; that basis is now superseded by a lower measurement. Any change should cite this number and be adjudicated by whether selected=true appears WITHOUT a rise in slot-gate-rejected-then-wrong outcomes. SCOPE LIMIT WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY: only command-shaped results are ever banked (REBIND_EXEC_FIELDS = command, cmd, script, sql), so for the two largest demand classes -- fs_edit, 67 calls, and code_modification_proposal, 55 calls -- there are ZERO donors and lexical rebind is structurally inapplicable rather than unlucky. It reports that as shape-mismatch x cache-size, which reads as 'many refusals' when it means 'this mechanism does not apply here'. DETECTION QUESTION (law 6): nothing measures this gate's admit rate or its own tally. The refusal distribution exists only as a console.log line and is invisible to the learning loop, so the system cannot notice that its adaptation mechanism has fired zero times in 24h -- an operator had to grep for it. Emitting the rebind outcome as a shaped impulse would let the loop grade its own adaptation attempts, which is the difference between a mechanism that learns and one that merely runs.
